title: iBT 2026 Paket 4 — Economics, Daily Life & Technical Interviews
theme: Behavioral nudges, refund policies, paragraph ordering, and professional email tasks.

passages.title: Daily Life Policy: Campus Conference Registration Refunds
passages.body:
Annual Undergraduate Research Symposium — Fee Policy:
Presenters pay a $25 registration fee covering lunch and printed abstracts. Cancellations submitted via the portal at least ten calendar days prior to May 2 receive a full refund minus a $3 processing charge. Within ten days of the event, refunds are unavailable, though presenters may transfer their slot to a co-author without penalty by emailing symposium@campus.edu.

passages.title: Default Choices in Household Energy Conservation
passages.body: Conventional public-utility campaigns often assume consumers adopt cleaner electricity plans purely after reading cost spreadsheets. Field experiments across mid-sized towns reveal a stronger behavioral lever: default enrollment. When municipalities set modest time-of-use conservation plans as the automatic option while letting households opt out via a single postcard, participation climbed from eighteen percent to over seventy-four percent. Economists attribute this gap to status-quo bias rather than indifference, since exit rates remained below five percent even one year later.

M: Why did switching from opt-in to opt-out quadruple clean-energy enrollment even though leaving took one stamp? Behavioral economists point to friction and status-quo bias—people stick with sensible defaults when no penalty blocks opting out. N: What drives high retention in default programs?

items.prompt: Listen to the economics talk. Why did default enrollment raise participation dramatically without coercion?
options: Many residents stick with pre-selected options when switching feels mildly effortful.
Utilities charged triple fees to anyone returning opt-out postcards.
Residents had no legal right to switch back later.
Advertisements ran continuously on local television.
items.answer: Many residents stick with pre-selected options when switching feels mildly effortful.
acceptedAnswers: Many residents stick with pre-selected options when switching feels mildly effortful.
items.explanation: Pembicara menjelaskan bias status-quo: masyarakat cenderung bertahan pada opsi bawaan saat opsi keluar tetap bebas dan mudah.

items.prompt: Write an Email (60–100 words): You are treasurer of the Economics Society and accidentally submitted an outdated receipt PDF in your reimbursement request to Student Activities (Ms. Brooks). Apologize concisely, explain that the corrected receipt is attached, and confirm the final total ($48.50).
items.explanation: Email harus jelas menyebutkan kesalahan dokumen lama, lampiran baru, dan angka pasti $48.50.

items.prompt: Write for an Academic Discussion (100–140 words): Prof. Chen asks: 'Should undergraduate economics courses focus more on real-world policy case studies even if it leaves less time for abstract mathematical proofs?' Clara favors case studies for career readiness; Ben argues mathematical foundations prevent shallow analysis. Share your stance.
items.explanation: Integrasikan kedua poin Clara dan Ben sambil merumuskan keseimbangan atau prioritas yang didukung alasan.

items.prompt: Take an Interview (Question 1 · ~45s): 'When managing personal finances as a student, is a fixed weekly budget or tracking every transaction in an app more helpful for you? Explain why.'
items.explanation: Pilih satu pendekatan, jelaskan alasannya secara praktis, dan beri satu contoh kebiasaan pribadi.

items.prompt: Take an Interview (Question 2 · ~45s): 'Do automatic reminders help people build sustainable habits, or do too many notifications eventually get ignored? Explain with an example.'
items.explanation: Beri perspektif bernuansa tentang manfaat awal vs kejenuhan notifikasi disertai contoh nyata.
